# 78 UI Kit — complete reference

> A theme-forward, no-build UI kit in plain HTML / CSS / JS. One stylesheet, one script, no dependencies.
> Every color resolves at runtime from CSS custom properties, so re-theming the components — *and* your
> Tabulator tables, FullCalendar calendars and Chart.js charts — is an override block, not a rebuild.
> MIT © 2026 James Robinson.

This file is the complete, copy-paste-ready reference: install, theming, every component with all of its
classes, variants, `data-*` attributes and JS options, the library adapters, and the theme generator API.
For a short index, read `llms.txt`. For the live gallery, see https://78uikit.com.

Version 0.x — the public API may still change before 1.0.

---

## Contents

1. Install
2. Theming — tokens, the mechanism, the theme toggle
3. Layout — the app shell

5. Cards, stat / KPI cards, grids and the meta line

15. Library adapters — Tabulator, FullCalendar, Chart.js
16. Theme generator — `_78.gen`
17. Events, storage keys and file map

## 1. Install

One stylesheet, one script, and an inline snippet that sets the theme before first paint.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">

  <!-- 1. PRE-PAINT THEME — first thing in <head>, before any stylesheet.
       Without it the page paints in the default theme and then snaps. -->
  <script>
  (function(){var p=localStorage.getItem('_78-theme')||'system';
  var t=p==='system'?(matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)').matches?'light':'dark'):p;
  var r=document.documentElement;r.dataset.theme=t;r.dataset.themePref=p;})();
  </script>

  <!-- 2. THE KIT -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/1978io/78UIKit@v0.3.0/css/kit.css">
  <script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/1978io/78UIKit@v0.3.0/js/_78.js"></script>

  <!-- 3. YOUR THEME OVERRIDES — after the kit, or they lose -->
  <style>
    :root[data-theme="dark"]  { --accent: #7c5cff; }
    :root[data-theme="light"] { --accent: #5b3df5; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  …
</body>
</html>
```

**Distribution.** `@v0.3.0` pins a release; `@main` tracks the latest and moves on every push. Minified
builds are served as `css/kit.min.css` and `js/_78.min.js`. Self-hosting is the same files at your own
path — the kit contains no absolute URLs.

**What `kit.css` pulls in.** `tokens.css`, `reset.css`, and every component stylesheet. Library adapters
are deliberately *not* imported: include only the ones you use.

**What `_78.js` does on load.** It wires every `._78-theme-toggle`, mounts every `._78-tabs`, mounts every
`._78-menu-wrap`, wires the app shell (`._78-nav-toggle`, `._78-nav-collapse`, `._78-scrim`), runs
`_78.viz.mountAll()` over the document, and delegates a click handler for `._78-alert-close`. It is safe
to load with `defer`, and all mounting is idempotent — calling a `mount` function twice does nothing.

**Markup added later.** After injecting HTML, re-mount just that subtree:

```js
_78.viz.mountAll(container);      // sparklines, progress, bars, donuts, trends
_78.tabs.mountAll(container);     // tab lists
_78.shell.mountMenus(container);  // dropdown menus
```

**The reset.** `reset.css` is minimal: `box-sizing: border-box`, zeroed margins, `body` painted with
`--bg` / `--text` / `--font`, block-level media, unstyled `button`, links in `--accent`, themed thin
scrollbars, a `:focus-visible` ring in `--accent`, and a `prefers-reduced-motion` block that neutralizes
animation. It styles `body`, so it is the one part of the kit that is not purely opt-in.

---

## 2. Theming

### 2.1 The rule

A theme is **only color**. Color tokens live in the `[data-theme]` blocks; everything else — radius, type
scale, spacing, control heights, layout widths, transitions — lives in a plain `:root` shared by every
theme. Nothing in the kit hardcodes a color; every component reads tokens. That is the entire theming
mechanism, and it is the only one: never fork `tokens.css`, override it.

### 2.2 The mechanism

```css
:root                            { /* non-color tokens, shared by every theme */ }
:root, :root[data-theme="dark"]  { color-scheme: dark;  /* color tokens */ }
:root[data-theme="light"]        { color-scheme: light; /* color tokens */ }
```

Bare `:root` carries the dark palette too, so the kit still looks right if JS never runs. `color-scheme`
is set per theme, so native scrollbars, form controls and the browser's own UI follow along.

The pre-paint snippet reads `localStorage['_78-theme']` (`"dark"` / `"light"` / `"system"`), resolves
`"system"` through `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)')`, and writes two attributes on `<html>`:

- `data-theme` — the **resolved** theme, `"dark"` or `"light"`. This is what the CSS keys off.
- `data-theme-pref` — the **preference**, `"dark"` / `"light"` / `"system"`. This is what the toggle icon
  keys off.

### 2.3 Overriding tokens

Put overrides in a stylesheet or `<style>` block loaded **after** `kit.css`. Only the tokens you actually
change need to be listed — everything else keeps its shipped default.

```html
<style>
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --accent: #7c5cff;
  --accent-hover: #9a80ff;
  --accent-text: #0f1117;
  --accent-lo: rgba(124, 92, 255, .16);
  --accent-lo-hover: rgba(124, 92, 255, .26);
  --accent-glow: 0 2px 10px rgba(124, 92, 255, .30);
  --ring: rgba(124, 92, 255, .35);
}
:root[data-theme="light"] {
  --accent: #5b3df5;
  --accent-hover: #4529d6;
  --accent-text: #ffffff;
  --accent-lo: rgba(91, 61, 245, .10);
  --accent-lo-hover: rgba(91, 61, 245, .18);
  --accent-glow: 0 2px 8px rgba(91, 61, 245, .25);
  --ring: rgba(91, 61, 245, .25);
}
</style>
```

Tokens cascade on any element, not just `:root`, so scoping one to a subtree re-themes just that subtree:

```html
<div class="_78-card" style="--accent: var(--info)">…</div>
```

### 2.4 The `-lo` tints

Every accent and semantic color ships a `-lo` companion: the same hue at low alpha, used as a
**background** under solid text in the full-strength color. This is why the kit never tints with
`opacity` — `opacity` washes out the label along with the fill.

```css
._78-badge-success { background: var(--success-lo); color: var(--success); }
```

### 2.5 Full token list

#### Core color — per theme

| Token | What it is |
|---|---|
| `--bg` | App background, the furthest-back surface |
| `--bg2` | Raised surface: cards, topbar, sidebar, modal, menu, toast |
| `--bg3` | Inset surface: inputs, badges, modal footer, empty states |
| `--border` | Every 1px edge, and the track behind progress / donut fills |
| `--text` | Primary text |
| `--dim` | Secondary text, icons, table headings, placeholders |
| `--accent` | The project's own color — the main per-project override |

#### Accent derived — per theme

| Token | What it is |
|---|---|
| `--accent-hover` | The accent's hover state (lighter on dark, darker on light) |
| `--accent-text` | Text drawn *on* an accent fill; must pass contrast against `--accent` |
| `--accent-lo` | Low-alpha accent tint, for fills behind accent-colored text |
| `--accent-lo-hover` | The tint's hover state |
| `--accent-glow` | The `box-shadow` on a primary button |

#### Semantic — per theme

`--success` · `--warn` · `--danger` · `--info`, each with a matching `-lo` tint (`--success-lo`,
`--warn-lo`, `--danger-lo`, `--info-lo`).

Semantic hues stay conventional — green / amber / red / blue — and deliberately never follow the accent.
A "themed red that isn't red" is a usability trap.

#### Categories — per theme

`--cat-1` … `--cat-6`, each with a `-lo` tint (`--cat-1-lo` …). Six label colors for things that are
**not states** — a source, a team, a type. Their hues (violet, teal, rose, olive, orchid, bronze) are
kept clear of the semantic hues so a category never reads as success / warn / danger, and like the
semantics they don't follow the accent. Each clears 4.5:1 as badge text on its own tint in both themes.
Use them in order: `cat-6` (bronze) is the one nearest a state (warn), so a short list never reaches it.

#### Charts — per theme

`--series-2` — the second series in a chart: a true gray that recedes behind `--accent` and, having no
hue, can never sit near it in hue whatever the accent is. It clears 3:1 on `--bg2` in both themes. The
Chart.js adapter uses it for the second dataset (§15.3); past two series it continues with `--cat-*`.

#### Surfaces, rows, focus — per theme

| Token | What it is |
|---|---|
| `--row-hover` | Table / menu / list row hover wash |
| `--row-border` | The lighter rule between table rows (vs. `--border` for the frame) |
| `--row-selected` | Selected row background; defaults to `var(--accent-lo)` |
| `--ring` | Focus ring color for form controls, drawn at `--ring-w` thickness |
| `--overlay` | The modal backdrop |
| `--shadow` | Resting elevation (cards) |
| `--shadow-lg` | Raised elevation (modal, toast, hovered card) |

#### Non-color — shared `:root`, one set for every theme

| Group | Tokens | Shipped values |
|---|---|---|
| Type | `--font`, `--font-mono` | Inter + system stack; `ui-monospace` stack |
| Type scale | `--fs-xs` `--fs-sm` `--fs-base` `--fs-lg` `--fs-xl`, `--lh` | 11 / 12 / 14 / 16 / 20px, 1.5 |
| Spacing | `--space-1` … `--space-6` | 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32px |
| Radii | `--radius-sm` `--radius` `--radius-lg` `--radius-pill` | 6 / 8 / 10 / 999px |
| Controls | `--control-h` `--control-h-sm` `--icon-btn-size` `--ring-w` | 36 / 28 / 32 / 3px |
| Layout | `--sidebar-w` `--rail-w` `--header-h` `--content-max` | 240 / 60 / 56 / 1120px |
| Motion | `--transition` `--transition-slow` | 140ms ease / 240ms ease |

### 2.6 `_78.theme` API

```js
_78.theme.pref              // getter → 'dark' | 'light' | 'system'
_78.theme.current           // getter → the resolved 'dark' | 'light'
_78.theme.set('light')      // set + persist + apply; returns the resolved theme
_78.theme.cycle()           // Dark → Light → System → Dark; returns the new preference
_78.theme.apply('dark')     // apply without persisting; returns the resolved theme
_78.theme.mount(el)         // wire an element as a toggle (idempotent)
_78.theme.KEY               // '_78-theme' — the localStorage key
_78.theme.PREPAINT          // the pre-paint snippet, as a string (for docs / tooling)
```

Free behavior: while the preference is `"system"` the page live-follows the OS setting, and a theme change
made in another tab is picked up through the `storage` event.

### 2.7 The `_78:themechange` event

Fires on `document` after every change, including the initial apply on load.

```js
document.addEventListener('_78:themechange', function (e) {
  console.log(e.detail.theme);   // 'dark' | 'light'  — resolved
  console.log(e.detail.pref);    // 'dark' | 'light' | 'system'
  myCanvasThing.redraw();        // the hook for anything that can't read CSS variables
});
```

Anything drawn to a `<canvas>` needs this event; anything drawn in CSS or SVG re-themes by itself.

### 2.8 The theme toggle

Any element carrying `._78-theme-toggle` is wired on load — no JS to write. Give it the three icons and
the CSS shows the one matching the current *preference*:

```html
<button class="_78-icon-btn _78-theme-toggle" type="button">
  <svg class="_78-theme-icon" data-pref="dark" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"
       stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M21 12.79A9 9 0 1 1 11.21 3 7 7 0 0 0 21 12.79z"/></svg>
  <svg class="_78-theme-icon" data-pref="light" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"
       stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4"/><path d="M12 2v2M12 20v2M4.9 4.9l1.4 1.4M17.7 17.7l1.4 1.4M2 12h2M20 12h2M4.9 19.1l1.4-1.4M17.7 6.3l1.4-1.4"/></svg>
  <svg class="_78-theme-icon" data-pref="system" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"
       stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="2" y="4" width="20" height="13" rx="2"/><path d="M8 21h8M12 17v4"/></svg>
</button>
```

`title` and `aria-label` are set and kept current by the kit. A toggle with no icons works too — it is
simply a button that cycles the theme.

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-theme-toggle` | Marks an element as a toggle; auto-wired on load |
| `._78-theme-icon` | An icon inside it; `data-pref="dark"` / `"light"` / `"system"` picks when it shows |

### 2.9 Tones — one vocabulary for every component

**This is the single list.** Every component that takes a tone takes the same names, and they are the
token names:

| Canonical | Token | Aliases (permanent) | Means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accent` | `--accent` | | Your brand color; a neutral highlight |
| `success` | `--success` | `green` | Done, healthy, up-is-good |
| `warn` | `--warn` | `amber`, `yellow` | Needs attention, not broken |
| `danger` | `--danger` | `red` | Failed, destructive, down-is-bad |
| `info` | `--info` | | Neutral information |
| `dim` | `--dim` | | De-emphasized; the plain look, stated |

Write the canonical name. The aliases exist so older markup keeps working and so a guess doesn't fail
silently; they are selector lists on the same rules, and they will not be removed.

| Component | Class or option | All six? |
|---|---|---|
| Badge | `._78-badge-{tone}` | yes |
| Tag | `._78-tag-{tone}` | yes |
| Text | `._78-text-{tone}`, or the short `._78-{tone}` | yes |
| Stat-card number | `._78-stat-card__num ._78-{tone}` | yes |
| Inline alert | `._78-alert-{tone}` | yes; `dim` is the plain alert |
| Data-viz (sparkline, progress, bar row, donut, figure, split bar) | `._78-tone-{tone}`, `data-tone` / `tone:` | yes |
| Modal | `._78-modal-{tone}`, `_78.modal.open({ tone })` | yes; `dim` is the plain modal |
| Toast | `_78.notify(msg, { type })`, `._78-toast-{tone}` | yes; `danger` is the same as the toast's own `error` |

In JS, `_78.tone(name)` returns the canonical name for any tone or alias, or `null`:

```js
_78.tone('red')      // → 'danger'
_78.tone('Amber')    // → 'warn'
_78.tone('brand')    // → null
_78.tone.names       // → ['accent', 'success', 'warn', 'danger', 'info', 'dim']
_78.tone.aliases     // → { green: 'success', red: 'danger', amber: 'warn', yellow: 'warn' }
```

**Categories** are a second, separate set for labels that are not states: `cat-1` … `cat-6`, on badge
(`._78-badge-cat-2`), tag, text (`._78-text-cat-2` / `._78-cat-2`) and viz tone (`._78-tone-cat-2`,
`data-tone="cat-2"`). Reach for a category when a status tone would lie — a trade source called "Scout"
shown in `warn` reads as a caution. `_78.tone('cat-2')` → `'cat-2'`; `_78.tone.categories` lists them.
Alerts, modals and toasts are about states, so they don't take categories.

```html
<span class="_78-badge _78-badge-cat-1">AI</span>
<span class="_78-badge _78-badge-cat-2">You</span>
<span class="_78-badge _78-badge-cat-3">Watch list</span>
```

Not tones, on purpose: button variants (`._78-btn-primary` / `-ghost` / `-danger` are actions, not
states), the score pill's `._78-high` / `-mid` / `-low` bands, and `._78-seg-accent` (a style for the
selected segment).

*(Added in 0.3.0. Before it, "danger" was `-red` on a badge and text but `-danger` on an alert; both
spellings now work on every component.)*

---

## 3. Layout — the app shell

A fixed topbar, an optional sidebar that collapses to an icon rail on desktop and becomes an off-canvas
drawer on mobile, and a main region that makes its own room for both. Because the topbar and sidebar are
`position: fixed` and nothing here styles `<body>`, **existing page content never has to be re-wrapped** —
add `._78-app-main` to your `<main>` and you are done.

### 3.1 Full markup

```html
<!-- In <head>, next to the theme snippet — ONLY on pages that have a sidebar -->
<script>
(function(){try{var s=localStorage.getItem('_78-sidebar');
document.documentElement.dataset.sidebar=s==='rail'?'rail':'full';}
catch(e){document.documentElement.dataset.sidebar='full';}})();
</script>

<header class="_78-topbar">
  <button class="_78-nav-toggle" aria-label="Toggle navigation">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"
         aria-hidden="true"><path d="M3 6h18M3 12h18M3 18h18"/></svg>
  </button>

  <a class="_78-topbar-brand" href="/">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true">…</svg>
    Your app
  </a>
  <span class="_78-topbar-sub">Production</span>

  <span class="_78-topbar-spacer"></span>

  <div class="_78-topbar-actions">
    <button class="_78-icon-btn _78-theme-toggle" type="button">…</button>

    <div class="_78-menu-wrap">
      <button class="_78-btn _78-btn-sm" id="acct-btn" aria-haspopup="true">
        <span class="_78-avatar">J</span>
        <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="14" height="14" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"
             stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 9l6 6 6-6"/></svg>
      </button>
      <div class="_78-menu" aria-labelledby="acct-btn">
        <a class="_78-menu-item" href="/account">Account</a>
        <a class="_78-menu-item" href="/settings">Settings</a>
        <div class="_78-menu-sep"></div>
        <a class="_78-menu-item _78-danger" href="/logout">Log out</a>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</header>

<aside class="_78-sidebar" aria-label="Primary">
  <nav class="_78-nav">
    <div class="_78-nav-heading">Overview</div>

    <a class="_78-nav-item _78-active" href="/">
      <span class="_78-nav-icon"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></span>
      <span class="_78-nav-label">Dashboard</span>
      <span class="_78-nav-badge">12</span>
    </a>
    <a class="_78-nav-item" href="/orders.php">
      <span class="_78-nav-icon"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></span>
      <span class="_78-nav-label">Orders</span>
    </a>

    <div class="_78-nav-heading">Admin</div>
    <a class="_78-nav-item" href="/users.php">
      <span class="_78-nav-icon"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></span>
      <span class="_78-nav-label">Users</span>
    </a>
  </nav>

  <span class="_78-nav-spacer"></span>

  <button class="_78-nav-item _78-nav-collapse" aria-label="Collapse sidebar">
    <span class="_78-nav-icon"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"
      stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15 18l-6-6 6-6"/></svg></span>
    <span class="_78-nav-label">Collapse</span>
  </button>
</aside>

<div class="_78-scrim"></div>

<main class="_78-app-main">
  <div class="_78-app-body">
    …your page…
  </div>
</main>
```

A topbar-only page is the same markup minus the `<aside>`, the `._78-scrim` and the sidebar pre-paint
snippet.

### 3.2 Classes

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-topbar` | Fixed header, `--header-h` tall, `--bg2` with a bottom border |
| `._78-topbar-brand` | Brand link — logo + name; turns accent on hover |
| `._78-topbar-sub` | A small dim label next to the brand (environment, tenant); hidden below 768px |
| `._78-topbar-spacer` | `flex: 1` — pushes everything after it to the right |
| `._78-topbar-actions` | Right-hand cluster: toggles, buttons, the account menu |
| `._78-nav-toggle` | The hamburger. Collapses to the rail on desktop, opens the drawer on mobile |
| `._78-sidebar` | Fixed sidebar, `--sidebar-w` wide, below the topbar, scrolls independently |
| `._78-nav` | Optional wrapper for the items (they also work as direct children) |
| `._78-nav-heading` | A section label above a group of items |
| `._78-nav-item` | One nav row: an `<a>` or a `<button>` |
| `._78-active` | On a `._78-nav-item`, the current page; also sets `aria-current="page"` |
| `._78-nav-icon` | Icon slot — required for the rail, which shows nothing else |
| `._78-nav-label` | The text; visually hidden (but still the accessible name) in the rail |
| `._78-nav-badge` | A count on the right of an item; becomes a corner dot in the rail |
| `._78-nav-spacer` | `flex: 1` — pushes what follows to the bottom of the sidebar |
| `._78-nav-collapse` | The bottom collapse button; its chevron rotates in the rail. Hidden on mobile |
| `._78-nav-tip` | The rail's hover / focus tooltip. Created by the kit — you never write it |
| `._78-scrim` | The mobile drawer's click-to-close backdrop; only rendered below 768px |
| `._78-app-main` | Put this on `<main>`: leaves room for the topbar and, if declared, the sidebar |
| `._78-app-body` | Inner wrapper: `--content-max` wide, centered, padded |
| `._78-avatar` | Small round accent-filled initial, for the account trigger |

### 3.3 State on `<html>`

State lives on the root element exactly like the theme, so it can be restored before the first paint.

| Attribute | Values | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `data-sidebar` | `"full"` \| `"rail"` | Desktop width. Persisted in `localStorage['_78-sidebar']` |
| `data-drawer` | `"open"` (or absent) | The mobile drawer. Runtime only, never persisted |

**The presence of `[data-sidebar]` is what reserves the sidebar's space in the CSS.** So:

- A page **with** a sidebar must run the sidebar pre-paint snippet. (`_78.shell` sets the attribute on
  load as a fallback — correct, but one frame late, which reads as a flash.)
- A page **without** a sidebar must *not* run it.

The mobile breakpoint is 768px, in both `components/shell.css` and `_78.shell.MOBILE`.

### 3.4 `_78.shell` API

```js
_78.shell.rail                  // getter → true when the sidebar is collapsed to the rail
_78.shell.drawer                // getter → true when the mobile drawer is open

_78.shell.setRail(true)         // collapse / expand; persists
_78.shell.toggleRail()
_78.shell.openDrawer()
_78.shell.closeDrawer()         // closeDrawer(false) skips returning focus to the trigger
_78.shell.toggleDrawer()
_78.shell.toggleNav()           // what the hamburger does: drawer on mobile, rail on desktop

_78.shell.setActive('/orders.php')   // see below
_78.shell.mountMenu(wrapEl)          // mount one ._78-menu-wrap
_78.shell.mountMenus(scope)          // mount every ._78-menu-wrap in a scope (default: document)
_78.shell.closeMenus()               // close every open dropdown

_78.shell.KEY                   // '_78-sidebar'
_78.shell.MOBILE                // 768
_78.shell.PREPAINT              // the sidebar pre-paint snippet, as a string
```

`setActive(match)` accepts, in order of precedence: an **element** (or any descendant of a nav item), an
**href written exactly as the item writes it** (which is how `'#reports'` resolves), a **CSS selector**,
or a **path** — matched on its last segment, so `location.pathname` finds the right item. It marks the
item `._78-active`, sets `aria-current="page"`, clears the others, and returns the element or `null`.

On load the kit marks the active item itself: whatever is hardcoded `._78-active` wins; if nothing is
marked, it falls back to `setActive(location.pathname)`.

### 3.5 Shell events

```js
document.addEventListener('_78:railchange',   e => console.log(e.detail.rail));   // true = collapsed
document.addEventListener('_78:drawerchange', e => console.log(e.detail.open));
```

These are the hook for anything that has to re-measure when the content width changes — a Tabulator
table, a Chart.js canvas, a virtualized list.

### 3.6 What you get for free

- The hamburger's `aria-expanded` answers "is the nav showing its labels?" — the drawer on mobile,
  full-vs-rail on desktop — and is kept in sync, including across resizes.
- In the rail, labels are visually hidden rather than removed, so each item keeps its accessible name, and
  they reappear as a hover / focus tooltip anchored to the rail's edge.
- Escape closes the drawer and any open menu; clicking the scrim closes the drawer; following a nav link
  closes it (without yanking focus back, because focus goes with the link); focus returns to the trigger
  on a normal close; growing past 768px closes a drawer that would otherwise be a stuck overlay.
- While the drawer is open, **focus stays in it**: Tab and Shift+Tab wrap around the drawer's visible
  controls, and the page behind is made `inert` so a screen reader's browse mode can't wander into it
  either. The topbar (which holds the toggle that closes the drawer) and the scrim stay live. Desktop full
  and rail modes are unaffected. *(Added in 0.3.0.)*
- `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the shell's transitions.

### 3.7 The nav is deliberately flat

Section headings group items; there are no nested or expandable sub-menus. If a section needs sub-pages,
they belong in the page — as tabs or in-page navigation — rather than in the sidebar.

---

## 4. Buttons and the segmented control

```html
<button class="_78-btn">Default</button>
<button class="_78-btn _78-btn-primary">Save changes</button>
<button class="_78-btn _78-btn-ghost">Cancel</button>
<button class="_78-btn _78-btn-danger">Delete</button>
<button class="_78-btn _78-btn-sm">Small</button>
<button class="_78-btn _78-btn-primary _78-btn-full">Full width</button>
<button class="_78-btn" disabled>Disabled</button>

<button class="_78-btn _78-btn-primary">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="16" height="16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"
       stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg>
  New order
</button>

<button class="_78-icon-btn" aria-label="Refresh">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true">…</svg>
</button>

<div class="_78-btn-group">
  <button class="_78-btn _78-btn-sm">Day</button>
  <button class="_78-btn _78-btn-sm">Week</button>
  <button class="_78-btn _78-btn-sm">Month</button>
</div>
```

| Class | Effect |
|---|---|
| `._78-btn` | Base: `--control-h` tall, `--bg2` fill, `--border` edge, gap for an icon |
| `._78-btn-primary` | Accent fill, `--accent-text` label, `--accent-glow` shadow |
| `._78-btn-ghost` | Transparent, dim label; accent tint + accent border on hover |
| `._78-btn-danger` | `--danger-lo` tint with a `--danger` edge and label; fills solid on hover |
| `._78-btn-sm` | `--control-h-sm` tall, smaller type and radius |
| `._78-btn-full` | `width: 100%` |
| `._78-icon-btn` | Square `--icon-btn-size` button, borderless until hovered. Give it an `aria-label` |
| `._78-btn-group` | Inline flex row of buttons with a gap; wraps |

`:disabled` and `[aria-disabled="true"]` both dim the button and block the press animation. An `<svg>`
inside `._78-icon-btn` is sized to 16px automatically. Focus is a 2px accent outline, offset 2px.

### 4.1 Segmented control — `._78-seg`

A joined run of buttons where **exactly one** is active: a range toggle, a chart type, a units switch. It
owns a *value*, not a panel — that is what separates it from `._78-tabs-segmented` (§9, bound to tab
panels) and from `._78-btn-group` (spaced, every button its own action).

```html
<div class="_78-seg" aria-label="Range">
  <button class="_78-seg-btn" data-value="1d">1D</button>
  <button class="_78-seg-btn" data-value="1w" aria-checked="true">1W</button>
  <button class="_78-seg-btn" data-value="1m">1M</button>
  <button class="_78-seg-btn" data-value="all" disabled>All</button>
</div>

<div class="_78-seg _78-seg-sm _78-seg-accent" aria-label="Side">
  <button class="_78-seg-btn">Buy</button>
  <button class="_78-seg-btn">Sell</button>
</div>

<div class="_78-seg _78-seg-full" aria-label="Chart type">
  <button class="_78-seg-btn">Line</button>
  <button class="_78-seg-btn">Bars</button>
  <button class="_78-seg-btn">Candles</button>
</div>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-seg` | The group: `--bg3` inset, `--border` edge, 3px padding, scrolls sideways if it overflows |
| `._78-seg-btn` | One option. The active one gets a `--bg2` raised surface and accent label |
| `._78-seg-sm` | Smaller: `--control-h-sm` height and `--fs-sm` type |
| `._78-seg-full` | Fills its container; every option gets an equal share |
| `._78-seg-accent` | The active option is an accent *fill* instead of a raised surface |

`_78.seg.mountAll()` runs on load over every `._78-seg`:

```js
var seg = _78.seg.mount(document.querySelector('._78-seg'));
seg.value       // '1w' — data-value, falling back to the button's text
seg.index       // 1
seg.select(2)   // select by index; select(2, true) also moves focus
seg.buttons     // the button elements
_78.seg.mountAll(container)   // after injecting markup
```

```js
document.addEventListener('_78:segchange', function (e) {
  e.detail;     // { index, button, value }  — bubbles from the ._78-seg group
});
```

**What the mount does.** `role="radiogroup"` on the group (it keeps a role you set yourself) and
`role="radio"` + `aria-checked` on each option — the ARIA for *exactly one of N*. Roving tabindex makes
the group a single tab stop; ←/→/↑/↓ move between options and **step over disabled ones**, Home / End go
to the first / last enabled option, and every change fires `_78:segchange`. The initial value is whichever
option carries `aria-checked="true"`, `aria-pressed="true"` or `._78-active`, else the first — and that
initial state does **not** fire an event. Mounting is idempotent; the mounted API is also on `el._78seg`.

Give the group an `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) saying what the value *is* — "Range", not "1D 1W
1M". A `._78-seg-btn` with no `type` is set to `type="button"`, so it is safe inside a `<form>`.

---

## 5. Cards, stat / KPI cards, grids and the meta line

### 5.1 Plain card

```html
<div class="_78-card">
  <div class="_78-card-head">
    <div class="_78-card-title">
      <span class="_78-eyebrow">Last 30 days</span>
      Revenue by channel
    </div>
    <button class="_78-btn _78-btn-sm _78-btn-ghost">Export</button>
  </div>

  …content…

  <div class="_78-card-foot">
    <span class="_78-text-dim _78-text-sm">Updated 4 minutes ago</span>
  </div>
</div>

<a class="_78-card _78-card-link" href="/reports">
  <div class="_78-card-title">Reports</div>
  <p class="_78-text-dim">Everything, sliced the way you asked for.</p>
</a>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-card` | `--bg2` surface, `--border` edge, `--radius-lg`, `--space-4` padding, `--shadow` |
| `._78-card-title` | `--fs-lg`, semibold; an `._78-eyebrow` inside it becomes its own line above |
| `._78-card-head` | Title on the left, actions on the right, on one row |
| `._78-card-foot` | Bottom action row. Full-bleed to the card's padding edges, like the modal foot, so its top border reaches both sides |
| `._78-card-foot-fill` | Adds the modal foot's `--bg3` surface to that row |
| `._78-card-link` | Makes the card an interactive link: accent border, lift and larger shadow on hover |
| `._78-card-grid` | Responsive grid of cards — `auto-fit`, min 200px per column |
| `._78-card-stack` | A vertical list of cards spaced by a `--space-4` gap (`-sm`: `--space-3`), wrapped or not |

Consecutive `._78-card` siblings get a `--space-4` gap automatically. Inside `._78-card-grid`, `._78-kpi-grid`,
`._78-flex` or `._78-flex-between` they don't: there the container's gap spaces them, and every card lines up
at the top. (In a grid of your own, set `margin-top: 0` on the cards yourself; the kit can't see it.)

**A list of cards — `._78-card-stack`.** A one-column grid with a `--space-4` gap (`._78-card-stack-sm`:
`--space-3`). Use it when the cards aren't direct siblings — each wrapped in a `<form>`, a partial that brings
its own wrapper, a hidden element between them — so the `+` rule can't reach them. Any child is spaced, card
or not; hidden children take no gap.

```html
<div class="_78-card-stack">
  <form><article class="_78-card"> … </article></form>
  <form><article class="_78-card"> … </article></form>
</div>
```

### 5.2 Stat / KPI card

The dashboard workhorse. Every part is optional — the label and the number alone are a valid card.

```html
<div class="_78-kpi-grid">

  <div class="_78-stat-card">
    <div class="_78-stat-card__head">
      <span class="_78-stat-card__label">Realized P/L</span>
      <span class="_78-stat-card__icon">
        <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"
             aria-hidden="true">…</svg>
      </span>
    </div>
    <div class="_78-stat-card__num _78-success">+$4,820</div>
    <div class="_78-stat-card__row">
      <span class="_78-stat-delta" data-delta="12.4"></span>
      <span class="_78-stat-card__sub">vs last month</span>
    </div>
    <div class="_78-stat-card__spark" data-values="18,22,19,27,31,29,34" data-tone="auto"></div>
  </div>

  <!-- "up is bad": drawdown, latency, spend, error rate -->
  <div class="_78-stat-card">
    <div class="_78-stat-card__label">Max drawdown</div>
    <div class="_78-stat-card__num _78-danger">-8.1%</div>
    <div class="_78-stat-card__row">
      <span class="_78-stat-delta _78-invert" data-delta="2.2"></span>
      <span class="_78-stat-card__sub">worse than last month</span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- a KPI that drills through -->
  <a class="_78-stat-card _78-card-link" href="/orders">
    <div class="_78-stat-card__label">Open orders</div>
    <div class="_78-stat-card__num">37</div>
    <div class="_78-stat-card__sub">6 awaiting fill</div>
  </a>

</div>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-stat-card` | Same surface as `._78-card`; combine with `._78-card-link` to make it clickable |
| `._78-stat-card__head` | Label on the left, icon on the right |
| `._78-stat-card__label` | Small uppercase dim label |
| `._78-stat-card__icon` | 28px accent-tinted rounded icon slot |
| `._78-stat-card__actions` | A control slot at the end of `__head` — a small toggle beside the label. A `._78-seg` inside drops to a 24px compact size, and the slot's negative block margin keeps the head at the label's height, so the number still lines up with its neighbors in a grid |
| `._78-stat-card__num` | The number: 28px, bold, tabular figures |
| `._78-stat-card__sub` | The caption under the number |
| `._78-stat-card__row` | Puts the delta and the caption on one baseline-aligned row |
| `._78-stat-card__spark` | Sparkline slot — full-bleed to the card's bottom edge, clipped to its radius |
| `._78-stat-card__lines` | Key : value lines under the number — a two-column grid, so every key shares a column and every value starts on the same edge |
| `._78-stat-card__line` | One line: a key and a value. In `__lines` it joins the grid; on its own it's a flex row |
| `._78-stat-card__key` | The key: `--fs-xs`, `--dim`, never wraps |
| `._78-stat-card__value` | The value: `--fs-sm`, `--text`, tabular figures. A `<b>` is the figure (add a short tone like `._78-success`), a `<small>` the dim aside after it |
| `._78-stat-delta` | The delta chip. Styled identically to `._78-trend`; see §12.6 |

**A control beside the label.** Put `._78-stat-card__actions` at the end of `._78-stat-card__head` — the
head centers its items when it holds one:

```html
<div class="_78-stat-card">
  <div class="_78-stat-card__head">
    <span class="_78-stat-card__label">Account value</span>
    <div class="_78-stat-card__actions">
      <div class="_78-seg" aria-label="Change measured against">
        <button class="_78-seg-btn" type="button" data-value="today" aria-checked="true">Today</button>
        <button class="_78-seg-btn" type="button" data-value="total">Total</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="_78-stat-card__num">$48,290</div>
</div>
```

**Key : value lines.** A label, then one or more figures, one row each:

```html
<div class="_78-stat-card">
  <div class="_78-stat-card__label">Account value</div>
  <div class="_78-stat-card__num">$48,290</div>
  <div class="_78-stat-card__lines">
    <div class="_78-stat-card__line">
      <span class="_78-stat-card__key">Account</span>
      <span class="_78-stat-card__value"><b class="_78-success">+$123.45</b> <small>today</small></span>
    </div>
    <div class="_78-stat-card__line">
      <span class="_78-stat-card__key">vs benchmark</span>
      <span class="_78-stat-card__value"><b class="_78-success">+0.50%</b> <small>you +1.2% · index +0.7%</small></span>
    </div>
    <div class="_78-stat-card__line">
      <span class="_78-stat-card__key">Trades</span>
      <span class="_78-stat-card__value"><b class="_78-danger">−0.30%</b> <small>on capital deployed, across 9 days</small></span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

Don't put a control inside `._78-stat-card__label` itself — the label is uppercase, letter-spaced text, and
its styling would reach the buttons.

Number color modifiers, applied to `._78-stat-card__num`: any tone from §2.9 in its short form (`._78-success`,
`._78-danger`, `._78-warn` …; the old `._78-green` / `._78-red` still work). With none the number is `--text`.

### 5.3 Grids

| Class | Layout |
|---|---|
| `._78-kpi-grid` | `auto-fit`, min 190px — the standard dashboard row, 2–6 across by width |
| `._78-kpi-grid-sm` | Same, min 150px — more, tighter cards |
| `._78-kpi-grid-lg` | Same, min 240px — fewer, roomier cards |
| `._78-card-grid` | `auto-fit`, min 200px — for `._78-card`s rather than KPIs |

Both use a `--space-4` gap and need no media queries.

### 5.4 Meta line — `._78-meta`

The small dim line of facts under a card headline: a scan summary, a thesis, the factors behind a score.
Each fact is a **child element** and the kit draws the `·` separator between them (with empty alt text, so
a screen reader doesn't read it), so the markup is a list of facts rather than a string with punctuation in
it.

```html
<div class="_78-card">
  <div class="_78-card-title">Watch list</div>
  <p class="_78-meta">
    <span class="_78-meta-label">Tonight's scan:</span>
    <span>Scanned <b>1,234</b> names</span>
    <span>read the top <b>20</b></span>
    <span>added <b>3</b></span>
  </p>
  …
</div>

<!-- one line, with an ellipsis, however long the text -->
<p class="_78-meta _78-meta-clamp">
  <span class="_78-meta-label">Watched for:</span>
  <span>a pullback to the 50-day average on falling volume, then a reclaim of…</span>
  <a href="/watch">Open the watch list →</a>
</p>
```

| Class / property | What it does |
|---|---|
| `._78-meta` | `--fs-sm`, `--dim`, tabular figures, wraps long words. A `·` before every child after the first |
| `._78-meta-label` | A lead-in ("Watched for:") — `--text`, semibold, and no separator after it |
| `b` / `strong` inside | A figure lifted out of the dim text: `--text`, semibold |
| `._78-meta-xs` | `--fs-xs` instead of `--fs-sm` — a tally line, a timestamp |
| `._78-meta-clamp` | Clamp to one line with an ellipsis |
| `._78-meta-clamp-2` | Clamp to two lines |
| `--_78-meta-lines` | With a clamp class: any number of lines, e.g. `style="--_78-meta-lines: 3"` |

Straight after a `._78-card-title` or `._78-card-head` it tucks up to `--space-1` under the title and keeps
`--space-3` below itself, so it reads as part of the heading. Text without child elements works too — it's
just a dim line with no drawn separators. A link inside it never breaks across lines.

---

## 6. Forms and the toggle switch

```html
<div class="_78-field">
  <label for="email">Email address</label>
  <input class="_78-input" id="email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com">
  <div class="_78-field-hint">We only use this for receipts.</div>
</div>

<div class="_78-field">
  <label for="market">Market</label>
  <select class="_78-select" id="market">
    <option>All markets</option>
    <option>Equities</option>
  </select>
</div>

<div class="_78-field">
  <label for="notes">Notes</label>
  <textarea class="_78-textarea" id="notes" rows="4"></textarea>
</div>

<!-- error state: aria-invalid does the styling, so the semantics can't drift -->
<div class="_78-field">
  <label for="qty">Quantity</label>
  <input class="_78-input" id="qty" value="0" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="qty-err">
  <div class="_78-field-error" id="qty-err">Quantity must be at least 1.</div>
</div>

<div class="_78-field-row">
  <div class="_78-field">
    <label for="from">From</label>
    <input class="_78-input" id="from" type="date">
  </div>
  <div class="_78-field">
    <label for="to">To</label>
    <input class="_78-input" id="to" type="date">
  </div>
</div>

<label class="_78-check">
  <input type="checkbox" checked>
  Email me when an order fills
</label>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-field` | Field wrapper with bottom margin; its `> label` is styled automatically |
| `._78-label` | Same label styling, when the label is not a direct child of the field |
| `._78-input` | Text-like input: full width, `--control-h` tall, `--bg3` fill |
| `._78-select` | Same box with the native arrow replaced by a token-colored chevron |
| `._78-textarea` | Same box, min 88px tall, vertically resizable |
| `._78-check` | Inline label wrapping a checkbox or radio; natives tinted with `accent-color` |
| `._78-field-hint` | Small dim helper text under the control |
| `._78-field-error` | Small `--danger` message under the control |
| `._78-field-row` | Flex row of fields, each `flex: 1 1 180px`; wraps on narrow screens |
| `._78-form-inline` | A field or two and the button that submits them on one row, bottoms aligned so the button sits level with the input; fields `flex: 1 1 180px` with no bottom margin, buttons / checks / switches keep their size; wraps on a phone |

**States.** Hover raises the border to `--dim`. Focus sets an `--accent` border plus a `--ring-w` ring in
`--ring`. `:disabled` dims and blocks the cursor. `[aria-invalid="true"]` (or `._78-invalid` on an input)
turns the border `--danger` and the focus ring `--danger-lo`. Placeholders render in `--dim`.

**A form in a card foot** — dismiss with a reason, an add-row, a quick filter. `._78-form-inline` inside
`._78-card-foot`; the foot already gives it the padding and the rule above:

```html
<div class="_78-card">
  <div class="_78-card-title">Northwind</div>
  <p class="_78-text-dim">Watched since Sep 14 for a renewal at the new price.</p>
  <div class="_78-card-foot">
    <form class="_78-form-inline">
      <div class="_78-field">
        <label for="dismiss-why">Why (optional)</label>
        <input class="_78-input" id="dismiss-why" name="reason" maxlength="500" autocomplete="off">
      </div>
      <button class="_78-btn" type="submit">Dismiss</button>
    </form>
  </div>
</div>
```

Put a hint or an error after the form rather than inside a field: a line under one input would push the
button out of line with it. A `._78-check` or `._78-switch` in the row centers on the input's line.

### 6.1 Toggle switch — `._78-switch`

A real `<input type="checkbox">` restyled as a track and a sliding thumb — not a `<div>` pretending. The
keyboard (Tab, then Space), the focus ring, `:disabled`, label association and the checked state are all
the native control's, so there is nothing to re-implement and nothing to get wrong.

```html
<label class="_78-switch">
  <input type="checkbox" role="switch" checked>
  <span class="_78-switch-label">Email me when an order fills</span>
</label>

<!-- small -->
<label class="_78-switch _78-switch-sm">
  <input type="checkbox" role="switch">
  <span class="_78-switch-label">Compact rows</span>
</label>

<!-- a settings row: label left, switch right -->
<label class="_78-switch _78-switch-row">
  <span class="_78-switch-label">Confirm before closing a position
    <span class="_78-switch-hint">Shows a modal every time.</span>
  </span>
  <input type="checkbox" role="switch" checked>
</label>

<!-- standalone (a table row, a toolbar): the input carries the class and its own name -->
<input class="_78-switch-input" type="checkbox" role="switch" aria-label="Live updates">

<!-- an external label works too -->
<label for="sw-live">Live updates</label>
<input class="_78-switch-input" id="sw-live" type="checkbox" role="switch">

<label class="_78-switch">
  <input type="checkbox" role="switch" checked disabled>
  <span class="_78-switch-label">Two-factor (enforced)</span>
</label>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-switch` | The wrapping `<label>`: inline flex, `--space-2` gap, pointer cursor |
| `._78-switch-input` | The checkbox itself, styled as the track + thumb. Optional inside `._78-switch` (a bare `input[type="checkbox"]` child is styled too), **required** when the switch stands alone |
| `._78-switch-label` | The text beside it |
| `._78-switch-hint` | A second, dim line under the label |
| `._78-switch-sm` | Small: a 28×16 track instead of 36×20. Goes on the wrapper or on a standalone input |
| `._78-switch-row` | Settings row: label left, switch pushed to the right edge, full width. Stacked rows space themselves `--space-4` apart |

**Stacked rows need no wrapper.** `._78-switch-row + ._78-switch-row` gets a `--space-4` top margin, like
stacked cards. Inside a `._78-flex-col` the rows drop that margin and the column's gap spaces them, so the
old `_78-flex-col _78-gap-16` wrapper looks exactly the same, and a different gap is still one wrapper
away. A margin utility on a row (`._78-mt-12`) still wins. *(Changed in 0.3.0; a wrapper of your own that
spaces rows with `gap` now gets the gap plus 16px, so drop one.)*

**Colors.** Off is a `--bg3` track with a `--border` edge and a `--dim` thumb; on is an `--accent` track
with an `--accent-text` thumb. Hover raises the edge to `--dim`, focus is the kit's 2px accent outline,
and `:disabled` dims the control (and its label) and blocks the cursor. Nothing is hardcoded — the switch
re-themes with everything else.

**Sizing** is three local custom properties on the input — `--switch-w`, `--switch-h`, `--switch-pad` — so
a one-off size is an inline override rather than new CSS: `style="--switch-w: 44px; --switch-h: 24px"`.

**`role="switch"`** is optional but recommended when the toggle takes effect immediately: a screen reader
then says "on" / "off" rather than "checked" / "not checked". It changes nothing about the styling. Use a
plain `._78-check` checkbox instead when the change only applies once a form is submitted.

---

## 7. Badges, tags, pills and the status line

```html
<span class="_78-badge">Draft</span>
<span class="_78-badge _78-badge-accent">New</span>
<span class="_78-badge _78-badge-success _78-badge-dot">Live</span>
<span class="_78-badge _78-badge-warn">Pending</span>
<span class="_78-badge _78-badge-danger">Failed</span>
<span class="_78-badge _78-badge-info">Beta</span>
<span class="_78-badge _78-badge-dim">Archived</span>

<span class="_78-tag">EUR/USD</span>
<span class="_78-tag _78-tag-accent">
  Momentum
  <button class="_78-tag-x" type="button" aria-label="Remove Momentum filter">×</button>
</span>

<span class="_78-score-pill _78-high">92</span>
<span class="_78-score-pill _78-mid">64</span>
<span class="_78-score-pill _78-low">28</span>

<span class="_78-eyebrow">Last 30 days</span>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-badge` | Small status chip: `--bg3` fill, `--border` edge, `--fs-xs`, semibold |
| `._78-badge-{tone}` | Any tone from §2.9 (`accent` `success` `warn` `danger` `info`, plus aliases): `-lo` tint fill with solid text, no border |
| `._78-badge-cat-1` … `-cat-6` | Categorical colors for labels that are not states (§2.9); same shape, `--cat-*` / `--cat-*-lo` |
| `._78-badge-dim` | Explicitly neutral (the base look, stated) |
| `._78-badge-dot` | Adds a 6px `currentColor` dot before the label — status that is not color-only |
| `._78-tag` | Softer pill for keywords / filters; `--fs-sm`, full text color |
| `._78-tag-{tone}` | Any tone from §2.9: a tinted tag |
| `._78-tag-x` | The remove control inside a tag (a `<button>` child is styled the same way) |
| `._78-score-pill` | Numeric pill, min 46px, bold, tabular figures |
| `._78-high` / `._78-mid` / `._78-low` | Score bands: success / warn / danger tint |
| `._78-eyebrow` | The small uppercase letter-spaced label above a title |

Every variant is a `-lo` tint plus solid text, never `opacity` — the label stays fully legible.

### 7.1 Status line — `._78-status`

A badge and the dim sentence that explains it — "Market: caution · half risk until the index reclaims its
50-day". Not an announcement bar: it sits in the flow and is only as wide as its content.

```html
<div class="_78-status">
  <span class="_78-badge _78-badge-warn">Market: caution</span>
  <span class="_78-status-text">half risk until the index reclaims its 50-day</span>
</div>

<!-- inside a sentence or a toolbar -->
<p>Sync <span class="_78-status _78-status-inline"><span class="_78-badge _78-badge-success">on</span><span class="_78-status-text">2 min ago</span></span></p>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-status` | Flex row, baseline-aligned, wraps; `--space-2` between badge and caption, `--space-1` between lines |
| `._78-status-text` | The caption: `--fs-sm`, `--dim`. Grows into the rest of the line; with less than ~14em left it drops to its own line instead of squeezing into a narrow column |
| `._78-status-inline` | `inline-flex`, and the caption only as wide as its text — for a status inside a sentence |

The badge (or a `._78-tag`) never wraps or shrinks. Any badge tone works, and `._78-badge-dot` keeps the
status readable without color. Put the full explanation in the caption, not only in a `title` — a
tooltip is invisible on a phone.

---

## 8. Table

`._78-table` styles a `<table>` you wrote by hand. For a real data grid — sorting, filtering, paging,
editing, virtual scroll — use Tabulator with the kit's adapter (§15.1); this does not try to replace one.

```html
<div class="_78-table-wrap">
  <table class="_78-table _78-table-striped">
    <caption>Filled orders, last 24 hours</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Symbol</th>
        <th>Side</th>
        <th class="_78-right">Quantity</th>
        <th class="_78-right">Fill price</th>
        <th class="_78-center">Status</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td>EURUSD</td>
        <td>Buy</td>
        <td class="_78-right">25,000</td>
        <td class="_78-right">1.0842</td>
        <td class="_78-center"><span class="_78-badge _78-badge-success _78-badge-dot">Filled</span></td>
      </tr>
      <tr class="_78-selected">
        <td>GBPUSD</td>
        <td>Sell</td>
        <td class="_78-right">10,000</td>
        <td class="_78-right">1.2711</td>
        <td class="_78-center"><span class="_78-badge _78-badge-warn">Partial</span></td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
    <tfoot>
      <tr>
        <td colspan="2">Total</td>
        <td class="_78-right">35,000</td>
        <td colspan="2"></td>
      </tr>
    </tfoot>
  </table>
</div>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-table` | Base: full width, collapsed borders, uppercase dim `<th>`, `--row-border` row rules |
| `._78-table-compact` | Tighter padding, for dense data |
| `._78-table-striped` | Zebra rows using `--bg3`, for long unbroken tables |
| `._78-table-sticky` | Sticky `<thead>` — needs a scroll container with a fixed height |
| `._78-table-wrap` | Bordered, rounded, `--bg2` scroll container: the table scrolls, never the page |
| `._78-selected` | On a `<tr>`: `--row-selected` background |
| `._78-right` | On a `<th>` or `<td>`: right-aligned with tabular figures — use it for numbers |
| `._78-center` | On a `<th>` or `<td>`: centered |

Rows hover to `--row-hover`, the last row drops its bottom rule, `<tfoot>` gets a top border and dim
semibold text, and `<caption>` renders as a small dim left-aligned line above the table.

---

## 9. Tabs

```html
<div class="_78-tabs">
  <button class="_78-tab" data-tab="panel-overview">Overview</button>
  <button class="_78-tab" data-tab="panel-activity">
    Activity <span class="_78-badge _78-badge-accent">3</span>
  </button>
  <button class="_78-tab" data-tab="panel-settings">Settings</button>
</div>

<div id="panel-overview">…</div>
<div id="panel-activity">…</div>
<div id="panel-settings">…</div>
```

`_78.js` mounts every `._78-tabs` on load. It sets `role="tablist"` / `role="tab"` / `role="tabpanel"`,
links each tab to its panel with `aria-controls` / `aria-labelledby`, gives tabs an id if they lack one,
adds `._78-tabpanel` to each panel, manages `aria-selected` and a roving `tabindex`, and hides inactive
panels with the `hidden` attribute. Activation is automatic — the panel follows focus.

| Class / attribute | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-tabs` | The tab list. Underline style; scrolls horizontally on narrow screens |
| `._78-tabs-segmented` | Pill variant: a bordered `--bg3` track with the selected tab raised |
| `._78-tab` | One tab. `data-tab="panel-id"` names its panel (`aria-controls` also works) |
| `._78-active` | On a tab in the markup: makes it the initially selected one |
| `._78-tabpanel` | The panel; added automatically. `[hidden]` panels are display-none |

**Keyboard:** Left / Right / Up / Down move between tabs (wrapping), Home selects the first, End the last.

**Initial selection:** whichever tab is marked `aria-selected="true"` or `._78-active`, else the first.

### 9.1 API and event

```js
var tabs = _78.tabs.mount(document.querySelector('._78-tabs'));
tabs.select(2);          // select by index; select(2, true) also moves focus
tabs.tabs;               // the array of tab elements
tabs.el;                 // the list element

_78.tabs.mountAll(scope) // mount every ._78-tabs in a scope (default: document)
```

`_78:tabchange` **bubbles from the tab list** (it is not a `document`-level event like the others):

```js
document.querySelector('._78-tabs').addEventListener('_78:tabchange', function (e) {
  console.log(e.detail.index, e.detail.id, e.detail.tab, e.detail.panel);
});
```

---

## 10. Dropdown menu

Built for the account menu in the topbar, but it works anywhere on the page.

```html
<div class="_78-menu-wrap">
  <button class="_78-btn _78-btn-sm" id="row-menu-btn" aria-haspopup="true">
    Actions
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="14" height="14" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"
         stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 9l6 6 6-6"/></svg>
  </button>

  <div class="_78-menu" aria-labelledby="row-menu-btn">
    <a class="_78-menu-item" href="/edit">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true">…</svg>
      Edit
    </a>
    <button class="_78-menu-item" type="button" onclick="duplicate()">Duplicate</button>
    <div class="_78-menu-sep"></div>
    <button class="_78-menu-item _78-danger" type="button" onclick="destroy()">Delete</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

The trigger is the element carrying `aria-haspopup`, or failing that the first `<button>` or `<a href>` in
the wrapper that is not inside the menu.

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-menu-wrap` | Positioning wrapper: trigger + menu. Auto-mounted on load |
| `._78-menu` | The popup panel — `--bg2`, bordered, `--shadow-lg`, right-aligned under the trigger |
| `._78-menu-left` | Left-align the panel instead |
| `._78-menu-item` | One row: an `<a>` or a `<button>`, with an optional leading 16px icon |
| `._78-danger` | On a menu item: `--danger` text and icon, for destructive actions |
| `._78-menu-sep` | A rule between groups; gets `role="separator"` |

**Free behavior:** click to open and to close; outside-click closes; Escape closes and returns focus;
choosing an item closes; Tab closes; Down / Up arrow from the trigger opens and lands on the first / last
item; Down / Up / Home / End move between items; only one menu is open at a time. The ids, `role="menu"`,
`role="menuitem"`, `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded` and the roving `tabindex` are all handled.

```js
_78.shell.mountMenu(wrapEl);      // mount one (for markup added later)
_78.shell.mountMenus(container);  // mount every one in a subtree
_78.shell.closeMenus();           // close them all
```

---

## 11. Notifications — the rule, not just the widgets

Pick by what the message *needs from the user*, not by how it looks:

| | Use for | Behavior | API |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Modal** | Needs acknowledgement — errors that stop the flow, confirms | Blocks; requires a click | `_78.modal.open()` / `.confirm()` / `.alert()` |
| **Toast** | Informational — "Saved", "Copied", "Export queued" | Auto-dismisses; never blocks | `_78.notify()` and `.success` / `.error` / `.warn` / `.info` |
| **Inline alert** | Tied to a region — form errors, empty states, a standing warning | Sits in the layout; persists | The `._78-alert` / `._78-empty` markup |
| **Quiet notes** | Worth knowing, nothing to do — "close to target", "earnings Thursday", why a button isn't there | Sits in a card; persists; never louder than the content | The `._78-notes` markup (§11.4) |

### 11.1 Modal

Always a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` — that is what buys the top layer, the `::backdrop`,
the focus trap and Escape. Body text is inserted with `textContent`; pass `html: true` (or a DOM node)
when you genuinely mean markup.

```js
// Everything at once
var choice = await _78.modal.open({
  title: 'Close this position?',
  body: 'This sends a market order immediately.\nSecond line, second paragraph.',
  size: 'sm',              // 'sm' | 'lg' | undefined (the 520px default)
  tone: 'danger',          // any tone (§2.9) — tints the title
  dismissible: true,       // false removes the × and blocks Escape/backdrop dismissal
  html: false,             // true = treat `body` as markup
  className: 'my-modal',   // extra classes on the <dialog>
  actions: [
    { label: 'Cancel',  value: null,    variant: 'ghost' },
    { label: 'Close it', value: 'close', variant: 'danger', autofocus: true }
  ]
});
// → the chosen action's `value`, or null if dismissed (Escape, backdrop, ×)
if (choice === 'close') submit();
```

`open(opts)` returns a `Promise`. With no `actions` it renders a single primary **OK** button whose value
is `true`. `variant` maps straight onto the button classes: `"primary"`, `"ghost"`, `"danger"`, or omitted
for the default button.

```js
// Confirm — resolves to a boolean: true only for the Confirm button,
// false for Cancel and for every dismissal (×, Escape, backdrop)
if (await _78.modal.confirm('Delete this saved view?', {
      title: 'Delete view',        // default: 'Are you sure?'
      confirmLabel: 'Delete',      // default: 'Confirm'
      cancelLabel: 'Keep it',      // default: 'Cancel'
      tone: 'danger',              // also makes the confirm button danger-variant
      size: 'sm'                   // default for confirm/alert
    })) {
  destroy();
}

// Alert — resolves to a boolean: true when OK was clicked, false when dismissed
if (await _78.modal.alert('Import finished. Reload to see the new rows?', {
      title: 'Import done',        // default: 'Heads up'
      okLabel: 'Reload',           // default: 'OK'
      tone: 'warn'
    })) {
  location.reload();
}
```

Both also accept `html` and `dismissible` (`false` = no ×, and Escape and the backdrop do nothing, so the
only way out is a button).

**Don't hang a side effect off a dismissal.** A promise that resolves whenever the dialog closes is not a
"yes". `_78.modal.alert(msg).then(reload)` reloads the page when the user presses Escape to get the alert
out of the way. Test the value (`if (await _78.modal.alert(msg)) reload()`), or better, do the side effect
because the *action* succeeded and use the alert only to report it.

*Changed in 0.3.0:* `alert()` used to resolve `undefined` however it closed; it now resolves `true` / `false`.
Callers that ignore the value are unaffected.

**Your own dialog markup**, driven by the same behavior:

```html
<dialog class="_78-modal" id="filters">
  <div class="_78-modal-head">
    <h2 class="_78-modal-title">Filters</h2>
    <form class="_78-modal-close" method="dialog">
      <button class="_78-icon-btn" value="" aria-label="Close">×</button>
    </form>
  </div>
  <div class="_78-modal-body">…</div>
  <div class="_78-modal-foot _78-modal-foot-split">
    <button class="_78-btn _78-btn-ghost">Reset</button>
    <button class="_78-btn _78-btn-primary">Apply</button>
  </div>
</dialog>
```

```js
_78.modal.mount(el);                  // add backdrop-click dismissal (idempotent);
                                      // data-_78-dismissible="false" on the <dialog> blocks
                                      // backdrop and Escape instead
var returnValue = await _78.modal.show(el);   // showModal() + resolve on close
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-modal` | The dialog: 520px, `--bg2`, `--radius-lg`, `--shadow-lg`, `--overlay` backdrop |
| `._78-modal-sm` / `._78-modal-lg` | 400px / 760px wide |
| `._78-modal-danger` / `._78-modal-warn` | Tone: colors the title |
| `._78-modal-head` | Title row with the close control |
| `._78-modal-title` | The heading (`open()` links it with `aria-labelledby`) |
| `._78-modal-body` | Scrolls past 60vh |
| `._78-modal-foot` | Right-aligned action row on a `--bg3` bar |
| `._78-modal-foot-split` | Pushes the first action to the left (a "Reset" opposite "Apply") |
| `._78-modal-close` | The `<form method="dialog">` wrapper for the × — closes with no JS |

**Headless-browser note:** Chrome in `--headless` mode only fires the `<dialog>` `close` event at a
rendering opportunity, so promise-based modal assertions read as flaky there. Verify modals headed.

### 11.2 Toast

```js
_78.notify('Copied to clipboard');

_78.notify.success('Order saved');
_78.notify.error('Could not reach the server');   // 6s instead of 4s, role="alert"
_78.notify.danger('Could not reach the server');  // the same thing, by its tone name
_78.notify.warn('Two rows were skipped');
_78.notify.info('Export queued');

var t = _78.notify('Uploading…', {
  type: 'info',        // any tone (§2.9), 'error' (= danger) or 'default'
  title: 'Import',     // optional bold line above the message
  duration: 0,         // ms; 0 = sticky, closable only by its × button
  html: false          // true = treat the message as markup (a DOM node also works)
});
t.close();             // dismiss it yourself
t.el;                  // the toast element
```

Defaults: 4000ms, or 6000ms for `error`. An error toast gets `role="alert"` + `aria-live="assertive"`;
everything else gets `role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"`. The container is created on first use.

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-toasts` | The fixed stack, bottom-right, created by the kit |
| `._78-toasts-left` / `._78-toasts-top` | Move the stack to another corner. The kit creates the container without them, so add the class yourself: `document.querySelector('._78-toasts').classList.add('_78-toasts-left')` — or, since the container is built on first use, target it in your own CSS |
| `._78-toast` | One toast: `--bg2`, `--shadow-lg`, a 3px left edge that carries the type |
| `._78-toast-success` / `-error` / `-warn` / `-info` | Type variants |
| `._78-toast-title` / `._78-toast-msg` / `._78-toast-body` / `._78-toast-close` | Its parts |

### 11.3 Inline alert and empty state

Pure CSS; the only behavior is dismissal, and that is delegated — any `._78-alert-close` removes its
alert.

```html
<div class="_78-alert _78-alert-danger" role="alert">
  <svg class="_78-alert-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"
       stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><path d="M12 8v5M12 16h.01"/></svg>
  <div class="_78-alert-body">
    <div class="_78-alert-title">Import failed</div>
    Three rows were rejected because their dates could not be parsed.
  </div>
  <button class="_78-alert-close" aria-label="Dismiss">×</button>
</div>

<div class="_78-alert _78-alert-info">
  <div class="_78-alert-body">Rates refresh every 15 minutes.</div>
</div>

<div class="_78-empty">
  <div class="_78-empty-title">No orders yet</div>
  <p>When you place one, it will show up here.</p>
  <button class="_78-btn _78-btn-primary _78-btn-sm">New order</button>
</div>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-alert` | Base: `--bg3`, bordered, with a 3px left edge in `--dim` |
| `._78-alert-{tone}` (any tone, §2.9) | `-lo` tint fill, colored left edge, colored title and icon |
| `._78-alert-icon` | 18px icon slot on the left |
| `._78-alert-body` | The text column |
| `._78-alert-title` | Bold first line |
| `._78-alert-close` | Optional dismiss button — wired by the kit, no JS to write |
| `._78-empty` | Centered dashed-border empty state |
| `._78-empty-title` | Its bold headline |

Add `role="alert"` yourself when the message appears in response to an action; a standing notice does not
need one.

**Lists in an alert** keep their indent and markers: a plain `<ul>` / `<ol>` inside `._78-alert-body` (and
inside a `._78-card`, `._78-modal-body` or `._78-details-body`) is indented `--space-5` with `--space-1`
between items. Use `._78-list-plain` (§14) for a list with no markers. *(Fixed in 0.3.0 — the reset used
to leave the bullets outside the box.)*

**Paragraphs in an alert** space themselves too: consecutive `<p>`s inside `._78-alert-body` get a
`--space-2` gap. Inside a `._78-card` or a `._78-details-body` it's `--space-3`, the same as a
`._78-modal-body`. The rule weighs nothing (`:where()`), so a margin utility on the paragraph wins. *(New in
0.4.0 — before, the reset ran two paragraphs together.)*

```html
<div class="_78-alert _78-alert-warn">
  <div class="_78-alert-body">
    <div class="_78-alert-title">Worth a look</div>
    <p>Earnings are due on Thursday, before the open.</p>
    <p>The position is past its time stop.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

```html
<div class="_78-alert _78-alert-danger">
  <div class="_78-alert-body">
    <div class="_78-alert-title">Three rows were rejected</div>
    <ul>
      <li>Row 7: unknown symbol</li>
      <li>Row 12: size is zero</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```

### 11.4 Quiet notes — `._78-notes`

The secondary text inside a card that an alert would shout: "close to target, nothing to do yet", the
time-stop and earnings lines under a position, the reason an action isn't offered. An alert is for something
to act on and `._78-empty` is for a region with nothing in it; notes are things worth knowing. Dim,
`--fs-sm`, and after other content in a card they sit `--space-4` down, where a card foot would.

```html
<!-- a heading and a list, as a footnote under the card's content -->
<div class="_78-notes _78-notes-ruled">
  <div class="_78-notes-title">Close to target, nothing to do yet:</div>
  <ul>
    <li>AAPL is 1.2% under its first target</li>
    <li>MSFT is 0.8% under its first target</li>
  </ul>
</div>

<!-- the compact alert: a quiet box, a toned edge, a tone per line -->
<div class="_78-notes _78-notes-box _78-tone-warn">
  <div class="_78-notes-title">Worth a look</div>
  <ul>
    <li>NVDA reports on Thursday, before the open</li>
    <li>AMD is past its 20-day time stop</li>
    <li class="_78-tone-info">The market check moved to caution</li>
  </ul>
  <p class="_78-notes-xs">Nothing has been changed. These are things to know, not instructions.</p>
</div>

<!-- "nothing to do, but here's why" — one line, in a card foot -->
<div class="_78-card-foot">
  <p class="_78-notes">No order to place: the price is already 3% past the entry.</p>
</div>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-notes` | The block (or a single `<p>`): `--dim`, `--fs-sm`. After other content in a `._78-card`, `--space-4` above it |
| `._78-notes-title` | An optional small heading: `--text`, semibold, sentence case |
| `<ul>` / `<ol>` inside | No bullets or indent of the prose kind; each `<li>` gets a 6px dot marker, `--space-1` apart |
| `._78-tone-{tone}` on an `<li>` | Colors that line's marker — any tone or category from §2.9. The text stays dim |
| `._78-tone-{tone}` on the block | Colors every marker (and the box edge); a tone on a line overrides it |
| `._78-notes-box` | The compact alert: `--bg3` inset, `--radius-sm`, a 3px left edge in the tone (`--border` without one) |
| `._78-notes-ruled` | A hairline above and `--space-3` of padding — a footnote under the card's content |
| `._78-notes-xs` | `--fs-xs` — on the block, or on one paragraph inside it |

Consecutive notes blocks sit `--space-2` apart. The marker is reinforcement, never the message: write the
line so it reads without its color.

---

## 12. Data-viz primitives — `_78.viz`, figure rows and split bars

Sparkline, progress bar, labeled bar row, donut / gauge, trend arrow, figure row and split bar — inline
SVG and plain elements painted with kit tokens, so a theme switch needs **no redraw**. They exist so you do
not load a chart library to draw one 40px trend line. Anything deeper — axes, tooltips, interaction — is
Chart.js and its adapter (§15.3).

**Color** flows through two inherited variables: `--viz` (the solid color, falling back to `--accent`)
and `--viz-lo` (its tint, falling back to `--accent-lo`). Set them with a tone class on the primitive
**or any ancestor**, or by hand:

| Tone class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `._78-tone-accent` | `--accent` / `--accent-lo` |
| `._78-tone-success` | `--success` / `--success-lo` |
| `._78-tone-warn` | `--warn` / `--warn-lo` |
| `._78-tone-danger` | `--danger` / `--danger-lo` |
| `._78-tone-info` | `--info` / `--info-lo` |
| `._78-tone-dim` | `--dim` / `--row-hover` |

Aliases (`._78-tone-green` / `-red` / `-amber` / `-yellow`) work too; see §2.9.

```html
<div class="_78-progress _78-tone-warn" data-pct="68"></div>
<div class="_78-donut" data-pct="41" style="--viz: var(--info); --viz-lo: var(--info-lo)"></div>
```

**Accessibility rule:** every primitive either renders its value as text or gets `role="img"` plus an
`aria-label`. Color or shape is never the only carrier of the meaning.

### 12.1 Auto-mounting

`_78.viz.mountAll()` runs on load over the whole document, and matches:

| Selector | Renders |
|---|---|
| `[data-values]` | A sparkline inside the element |
| `._78-progress[data-pct]` | Progress track + fill + `role="progressbar"` |
| `._78-bar-row[data-pct]` | Bar fill + `role="progressbar"` |
| `._78-donut[data-pct]` | The ring and its center value |
| `._78-split-bar` | Sizes its `._78-split-seg` children and writes the group `aria-label` |
| `._78-trend[data-delta]`, `._78-stat-delta[data-delta]` | The arrow, the text and the direction word |

Call `_78.viz.mountAll(container)` after injecting markup. Every function is also callable directly, and
re-rendering an element replaces its previous SVG rather than stacking a second one.

### 12.2 Sparkline

```html
<!-- auto-mounted -->
<div class="_78-stat-card__spark" data-values="18,22,19,27,31,29,34" data-tone="auto"></div>
<div data-values="4 7 6 9 12" data-fill="false" data-dot="true" data-label="Signups, last 5 days"></div>
```

```js
_78.viz.sparkline(el, [18, 22, 19, 27, 31], {
  width: 120,      // viewBox width  (default 120) — the SVG still stretches to the container
  height: 32,      // viewBox height (default 32)
  fill: true,      // the area under the line (default true)
  dot: false,      // the dot on the last point (default FALSE — opt in with dot:true)
  tone: 'auto',    // a tone name, or 'auto': success if the series ends up, danger if down
  label: 'Revenue, 7 days'   // aria-label + <title>
});
```

`data` may be an array or a string of numbers separated by commas or whitespace; omit it and the element's
`data-values` is used. Fewer than two points renders nothing (returns `null`). A flat series draws down
the middle instead of dividing by zero. The stroke is non-scaling, so a stretched sparkline does not get a
fat line.

Attributes: `data-values`, `data-tone` (including `"auto"`), `data-label`, `data-fill="false"`,
`data-dot="true"`.

The end-of-series dot is **off by default** (it crowds a small card); `dot: true` / `data-dot="true"` turns
it on. *(Changed in 0.2.0 — it used to be on by default.)* The dot stays round at any width: it is a
zero-length path drawn by its round cap with a non-scaling stroke, so its color is `stroke` and its size is
`stroke-width` (5px, with an 8px `--bg2` halo underneath). *(Changed in 0.3.0 — it was a `<circle>`, which
stretched into an ellipse in any container wider than 120px. A custom rule that set `fill` on
`._78-sparkline-dot` should set `stroke` now.)*

Without a label, the kit writes a plain-English one: *"Trend, 7 points: 18 to 34 (up)"*.

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-sparkline` | The generated `<svg>`: full width, 32px tall |
| `._78-sparkline-line` / `-area` / `-dot` / `-base` | Its parts, all painted from `--viz` / `--viz-lo` |
| `._78-sparkline-dot-ring` | The `--bg2` halo drawn under the end dot |

### 12.3 Progress bar

```html
<div class="_78-progress" data-pct="72">
  <div class="_78-progress-head">
    <span class="_78-progress-label">Win rate</span>
    <span class="_78-progress-value"></span>   <!-- left empty: filled in as "72%" -->
  </div>
  <div class="_78-progress-track"><div class="_78-progress-fill"></div></div>
</div>

<!-- the minimum: track and fill are created for you -->
<div class="_78-progress _78-tone-warn _78-progress-lg" data-pct="68" data-label="Margin used"></div>
```

```js
_78.viz.progress(el, 72, {
  label: 'Win rate',   // aria-label; falls back to data-label, then ._78-progress-label's text
  text: true           // false leaves ._78-progress-value alone instead of writing "72%"
});
```

The percentage is clamped to 0–100. The track gets `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow` / `min` /
`max`. An existing `._78-progress-value` with text in it is never overwritten.

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-progress` | The wrapper — carry `data-pct` here |
| `._78-progress-head` | Label row above the bar |
| `._78-progress-label` / `._78-progress-value` | Its dim label and its bold tabular value |
| `._78-progress-track` / `._78-progress-fill` | The 6px rail and its `--viz` fill (created if absent) |
| `._78-progress-sm` / `._78-progress-lg` | 4px / 10px rail instead |

### 12.4 Bar row

For ranked lists. Unlike progress, the `._78-bar-track` element must exist in your markup — the row is a
three-column grid, so the kit does not guess where it goes.

```html
<div class="_78-bar-list">
  <div class="_78-bar-row" data-pct="82">
    <span class="_78-bar-label">EUR/USD</span>
    <span class="_78-bar-track"><span class="_78-bar-fill"></span></span>
    <span class="_78-bar-value">82</span>
  </div>
  <div class="_78-bar-row _78-tone-info" data-pct="47">
    <span class="_78-bar-label">GBP/USD</span>
    <span class="_78-bar-track"></span>
    <span class="_78-bar-value">47</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

```js
_78.viz.bar(el, 82, { label: 'EUR/USD' });   // label falls back to ._78-bar-label's text
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-bar-list` | Vertical stack of rows with a gap |
| `._78-bar-row` | Grid: label (min 72px / 26%) · track · value. Carry `data-pct` here |
| `._78-bar-label` | Truncates with an ellipsis |
| `._78-bar-track` / `._78-bar-fill` | The 8px rail and its `--viz` fill (the fill is created if absent) |
| `._78-bar-value` | Right-aligned, bold, tabular |

### 12.5 Donut and gauge

```html
<div class="_78-donut" data-pct="68" data-label="Margin used"></div>
<div class="_78-donut _78-gauge _78-tone-success" data-pct="41" data-label="Health"></div>
<div class="_78-donut _78-donut-lg" data-pct="92"></div>

<!-- supply your own center content and it is respected -->
<div class="_78-donut" data-pct="76">
  <div class="_78-donut-center">
    <div class="_78-donut-value">3.4×</div>
    <div class="_78-donut-label">Leverage</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```js
_78.viz.donut(el, 68, {
  size: 100,           // viewBox size (default 100)
  stroke: 12,          // ring thickness (default 12, or 11 for a gauge)
  gauge: false,        // true forces the 240° arc; otherwise ._78-gauge decides
  label: 'Margin used',
  value: '68%'         // override the center text (default: the rounded percentage)
});
```

A gauge is the same ring drawn as a 240° arc with the gap at the bottom and the value sitting in it. The
wrapper gets `role="img"` and an `aria-label` of `"<label>: <value>"`; the SVG itself is `aria-hidden`.

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-donut` | The wrapper — 104px wide. Carry `data-pct` here |
| `._78-gauge` | Draws the ring as a 240° arc |
| `._78-donut-sm` / `._78-donut-lg` | 72px / 136px wide, with the value type scaled to match |
| `._78-donut-center` / `._78-donut-value` / `._78-donut-label` | Center stack (created if absent) |
| `._78-donut-track` / `._78-donut-fill` | The ring's two circles: `--border` and `--viz` |

### 12.6 Trend arrow

```html
<span class="_78-trend" data-delta="12.4"></span>              <!-- ▲ +12.4% in green -->
<span class="_78-trend" data-delta="-3.1"></span>              <!-- ▼ -3.1%  in red   -->
<span class="_78-trend" data-delta="0"></span>                 <!-- – 0%     in dim   -->
<span class="_78-trend _78-trend-pill" data-delta="8.2" data-unit=" bps"></span>
<span class="_78-stat-delta" data-delta="2.2" data-invert="true"></span>   <!-- up is bad -->

<!-- markup-only, no JS -->
<span class="_78-trend _78-up">▲ 12.4% <span class="_78-sr-only">up</span></span>
```

```js
_78.viz.trend(el, 12.4, {
  invert: false,     // true = up is bad: colors up red and down green
  unit: '%',         // '' for none; data-unit="" also means none
  text: '+12.4%',    // override the rendered text entirely
  label: 'up'        // the screen-reader word (default: 'up' / 'down' / 'no change')
});
```

Direction comes from the number's sign, with exactly `0` reading as flat. The kit renders an arrow SVG,
the text, and a `._78-sr-only` direction word — so the meaning survives without color or shape.

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-trend` | The chip. `._78-stat-delta` is identical, for use inside a stat card |
| `._78-up` / `._78-down` / `._78-flat` | Direction — set by `_78.viz.trend()`, or write it yourself |
| `._78-invert` | Up is bad: swaps the success / danger colors |
| `._78-trend-pill` | Pill treatment, with a tinted background per direction |

Attributes: `data-delta`, `data-unit`, `data-invert="true"`.

### 12.7 Figure row — `._78-figure-row`

N *related* numbers read side by side, each with a label and a semantic tone shown as a colored left edge:
entry / take-profit / stop, plan / actual / variance, min / median / max, three-tier pricing. One fact in
parts — where a `._78-kpi-grid` (§5.3) is unrelated metrics and a `._78-stat-card` is one headline number.
CSS only, and toned with the same `._78-tone-*` classes as everything else in this section, so a figure
and the chart beside it agree on color.

```html
<div class="_78-figure-row">
  <div class="_78-figure _78-tone-accent">
    <span class="_78-figure-label">Entry</span>
    <span class="_78-figure-value">1.0842</span>
  </div>
  <div class="_78-figure _78-tone-success">
    <span class="_78-figure-label">Take profit</span>
    <span class="_78-figure-value">1.0985</span>
    <span class="_78-figure-sub">+143 pips</span>
  </div>
  <div class="_78-figure _78-tone-danger">
    <span class="_78-figure-label">Stop</span>
    <span class="_78-figure-value">1.0790</span>
    <span class="_78-figure-sub">−52 pips</span>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- the value itself carries the tone, in a denser row -->
<div class="_78-figure-row _78-figure-row-sm _78-figure-strong"> … </div>

<!-- no fill: the tone moves to the label -->
<div class="_78-figure-row _78-figure-row-plain"> … </div>

<!-- one figure that isn't part of the set's meaning: no tone, a plain --border edge -->
<div class="_78-figure-row">
  <div class="_78-figure _78-tone-success"> … Signal when … </div>
  <div class="_78-figure _78-tone-danger"> … Dead if … </div>
  <div class="_78-figure _78-figure-neutral">
    <span class="_78-figure-label">Time left</span>
    <span class="_78-figure-value">6</span>
    <span class="_78-figure-sub">trading days</span>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- a whole row with no semantic edges (any ._78-tone-* inside is ignored) -->
<div class="_78-figure-row _78-figure-row-neutral"> … </div>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-figure-row` | The row: an auto-fit grid, min 140px per figure, `--space-3` gap, wraps |
| `._78-figure` | One figure: `--bg3` fill, `--radius-sm`, and a 3px `--viz` left edge |
