| `._78-figure-label` | The uppercase `--fs-xs` label — always say what the number is |
| `._78-figure-value` | The number: `--fs-lg`, bold, tabular figures |
| `._78-figure-sub` | A small dim line under the value |
| `._78-figure-strong` | On a figure (or the row): the value takes the tone color too |
| `._78-figure-row-sm` | Denser padding and an `--fs-base` value, for a table cell or a narrow card |
| `._78-figure-row-plain` | No fill and no edge; the tone moves to the label |
| `._78-figure-neutral` | On one figure: no tone, even one inherited from the row or a parent — the edge is `--border`, a `-strong` value is `--text`, a `-plain` label is `--dim`. For a figure that isn't part of the set's meaning ("Time left" beside a target and a stop) |
| `._78-figure-row-neutral` | On the row: every figure neutral, so the row carries no semantic edges at all |

A figure with no tone class already has a `--border` edge; `-neutral` is for when a tone would otherwise be
inherited, and for saying so in the markup.

The label is the meaning and the color is reinforcement — never ship a figure row whose only difference
between parts is the tone.

### 12.8 Split bar — `._78-split-bar`

One bar, two or more proportional segments, each with its own semantic color: risk vs reward, spent vs
remaining, pass / skip / fail. `._78-progress` (§12.3) is a single fill of one track and `._78-bar-row`
(§12.4) is one row of a ranked list; this is the split of a whole into named parts.

```html
<div class="_78-split-head">
  <span class="_78-split-title">Risk / reward</span>
  <span class="_78-split-total">1 : 1.9</span>
</div>
<div class="_78-split-bar" data-label="Risk versus reward">
  <span class="_78-split-seg _78-tone-danger"  data-pct="35" data-label="Risk"></span>
  <span class="_78-split-seg _78-tone-success" data-pct="65" data-label="Reward"></span>
</div>
<div class="_78-split-legend">
  <span class="_78-split-key _78-tone-danger">Risk <b>35%</b></span>
  <span class="_78-split-key _78-tone-success">Reward <b>65%</b></span>
</div>
```

```js
_78.viz.splitBar(el, [
  { pct: 45, tone: 'accent', label: 'Equities' },
  { pct: 30, tone: 'info',   label: 'FX' },
  { pct: 25, tone: 'dim',    label: 'Cash' }
], { label: 'Allocation' });        // omit the array to size the markup that is already there
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-split-bar` | The track: 8px tall, pill radius, `--border` fill, a 2px gap between segments |
| `._78-split-seg` | One segment, painted from `--viz`; its width is set by `_78.viz.splitBar()` |
| `._78-split-bar-sm` / `-lg` | 4px / 12px tall |
| `._78-split-head` | Optional title + total line above the bar |
| `._78-split-title` / `._78-split-total` | Its two halves — dim label, solid tabular value |
| `._78-split-legend` | A wrapping row of keys under the bar |
| `._78-split-key` | One key: takes the segment's tone class and gets a matching dot |

Attributes: `data-pct` and `data-label` per segment, `data-label` on the bar itself.

**Totals.** Values under 100 leave the shortfall as visible track, so "68% used" works with one segment.
Values totaling more than 100 are treated as raw amounts and shared out — `512 / 96 / 32` renders as 80% /
15% / 5% with no math on your side.

**Accessibility.** The bar becomes one `role="img"` whose `aria-label` names every segment and its share
("Risk versus reward: Risk 35%, Reward 65%"), and each segment repeats its own text as a `title`. Write
the legend yourself — the wording is yours, and it is what makes the colors legible.

---

## 13. Disclosure — `._78-details`

A styled `<details>` / `<summary>`: the native marker is removed (including Safari's
`::-webkit-details-marker`) and replaced with a chevron that rotates when the element opens. **No JS** —
the keyboard, screen-reader, and find-in-page behavior is the browser's own. This is the progressive
"show the numbers behind this" pattern: the headline stays readable, the detail is one click away.

```html
<details class="_78-details">
  <summary>Show the numbers behind this <span class="_78-details-meta">3 legs</span></summary>
  <div class="_78-details-body">
    …
  </div>
</details>

<details class="_78-details _78-details-fill" open>
  <summary>Assumptions</summary>
  <div class="_78-details-body">Commission at 0.08%, financing at base + 2.5%.</div>
</details>

<details class="_78-details _78-details-plain">
  <summary>What counts as an open position?</summary>
  <div class="_78-details-body _78-text-sm">Anything with a non-zero quantity at the close.</div>
</details>
```

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `._78-details` | The `<details>`: `--bg2` surface, `--border` edge, `--radius`, clipped corners |
| `._78-details-summary` | Optional class on the `<summary>` — a direct `> summary` is styled anyway |
| `._78-details-meta` | Pushed to the right of the summary: a count, a total, a badge |
| `._78-details-body` | The revealed content: `--space-3` padding, separated by a top border |
| `._78-details-plain` | No box — for a disclosure inside a card that already has one |
| `._78-details-fill` | `--bg3` summary bar, the way a table or a card foot is tinted |
| `._78-details-sm` | Smaller type and padding throughout |

The chevron is pure CSS (two borders rotated), so there is no icon set to load and it follows the text
color; `[open]` rotates it. Hover tints the summary with `--row-hover` and turns it accent; focus is the
kit's 2px accent outline, inset. Consecutive `._78-details` siblings get a `--space-2` gap.

Keep the summary a real summary — a sentence someone can act on. Screen readers announce it as a
disclosure with its expanded state for free.

---

## 14. Utilities

A deliberately small set — the kit is a component library, not a utility framework.

| Group | Classes |
|---|---|
| Text | `._78-text-{tone}` and the short `._78-{tone}` (all six tones and their aliases, §2.9) · `._78-text-sm` `._78-text-xs` |
| Type | `._78-fw-600` `._78-mono` `._78-nums` (tabular figures) `._78-truncate` |
| Layout | `._78-flex` `._78-flex-between` `._78-flex-wrap` `._78-flex-col` `._78-grow` |
| Gaps | `._78-gap-8` `._78-gap-12` `._78-gap-16` |
| Margins | `._78-mt-8` `._78-mt-12` `._78-mt-16` `._78-mb-4` `._78-mb-8` `._78-mb-12` `._78-mb-16` |
| Lists | `._78-list-plain` |
| Accessibility | `._78-sr-only` |

`._78-flex` and `._78-flex-between` both center their items vertically.

**Lists.** The reset strips list padding everywhere, on purpose. Inside the components that hold prose
(`._78-alert-body`, `._78-card`, `._78-modal-body`, `._78-details-body`) a `<ul>` / `<ol>` with **no
class of its own** gets an indent and a rhythm back; everywhere else lists stay bare. The rule is written
with `:where()`, so any rule of yours out-ranks it. `._78-list-plain` removes markers and indent anywhere
(if your own prose CSS styles a bare `.content ul`, scope it as `ul:not([class])` or it will out-rank the
utility):

```html
<ul class="_78-list-plain">
  <li>No markers, no indent, still a list to a screen reader</li>
</ul>
```

**Paragraphs.** The reset zeroes paragraph margins too. In the same components, a `<p>` that follows a
`<p>` gets a top margin back: `--space-2` in `._78-alert-body`, `--space-3` in `._78-card` and
`._78-details-body` (`._78-modal-body` has always had `--space-3`). Zero specificity, so a utility such as
`._78-mt-8` on the paragraph, or any rule of yours, wins.

**Two spellings, one color.** Every text tone has a long and a short form — `._78-text-danger` and
`._78-danger` are the same rule, for all six tones and their aliases (§2.9). The short forms started life
on `._78-stat-card__num` and now work anywhere, so no spelling is a typo.

**The escape hatch.** There is deliberately no margin utility above 16px and there are no padding
utilities. Above the scale, use the space tokens directly — `style="padding: var(--space-5)"` — that is
the intended way out, not a gap in the set.

### 14.1 JS helpers — `_78.util`

Two small helpers, dependency-free and DOM-free. *(Added in 0.3.0.)*

**`_78.util.sortAlpha(a, b)`** — a comparator for human sorting. Case-insensitive, locale-aware
(`Intl.Collator` with `numeric: true`), so "Item 2" sorts before "Item 10". Blanks (`null`,
`undefined`, `""`) sort after everything else; non-strings are compared as their text.

```js
['Item 10', 'item 2', 'Item 1', 'apple', 'Banana'].sort(_78.util.sortAlpha)
// → ['apple', 'Banana', 'Item 1', 'item 2', 'Item 10']

new Tabulator('#grid', {
  columns: [{ title: 'Name', field: 'name', sorter: _78.util.sortAlpha }]   // works as-is
});
```

**`_78.util.duration(ms, opts)`** — milliseconds as plain English.

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `long` | `false` | `true` spells units out: "2 hours 5 minutes" instead of "2 hrs 5 min" |
| `parts` | `2` | The most units to show: `1` → "3 days", `3` → "3 days 4 hrs 50 min" |

| Input (ms) | Output |
|---|---|
| `0` | `"0 sec"` |
| `400` (or `-400`) | `"< 1 sec"` |
| `45000` | `"45 sec"` |
| `59600` | `"1 min"` (rounded, with carry) |
| `90000` | `"1 min 30 sec"` |
| `7500000` | `"2 hrs 5 min"` |
| `7220000` | `"2 hrs"` (a part that rounds to 0 is left out — never "0 min") |
| `259200000` | `"3 days"` |
| `-180000` | `"-3 min"` |
| `1e12` | `"11,574 days 2 hrs"` (days are the largest unit) |
| `NaN`, `"abc"` | `""` |

Numeric strings are accepted (`"7500000"` → `"2 hrs 5 min"`). Singular units are singular: "1 hr",
"1 day", "1 minute".

---

## 15. Library adapters

*Your tables and charts match your theme automatically, including when it switches.* Adapters are
**opt-in** — never part of `kit.css` — and **nothing is vendored**: you bring your own copy of each
library, at your own version. Always load an adapter **after** the library it themes.

### 15.1 Tabulator (6.x, verified against 6.5.2)

```html
<!-- verified against Tabulator 6.5.2 -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tabulator-tables@6.5.2/dist/css/tabulator.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/1978io/78UIKit@v0.3.0/css/adapters/tabulator.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tabulator-tables@6.5.2/dist/js/tabulator.min.js"></script>
```

Pure CSS: it maps Tabulator's classes onto kit tokens — frame and header to `--bg2`, cells to `--text`,
row rules to `--row-border`, hover to `--row-hover`, selection to `--row-selected`, sorters, editors,
filters, the pagination controls and the column resize handles to `--accent`. The table re-themes the
moment `data-theme` flips, with no JS and no redraw. Tabulator renames classes across majors, so re-check
the adapter on a major upgrade.

**Responsive collapse** (`responsiveLayout: 'collapse'`) is themed too. The fold-out panel under each row
wraps long values inside the table's width; Tabulator's cells are `nowrap`, which the panel would
otherwise inherit. The +/- toggle is an `--accent` glyph on an `--accent-lo` tint in both themes
(Tabulator hardcodes a white stroke; the adapter switches it to `currentColor`). The panel's text is
`--fs-base`, the same as the cells, so it follows a changed type scale.

```js
new Tabulator('#accounts', {
  layout: 'fitColumns',
  responsiveLayout: 'collapse',
  responsiveLayoutCollapseStartOpen: false,
  columns: [
    { formatter: 'responsiveCollapse', width: 40, minWidth: 40, hozAlign: 'center',
      resizable: false, headerSort: false },                               // the +/- toggle, first
    { title: 'Customer', field: 'customer', minWidth: 120, responsive: 0 }, // never collapses
    { title: 'Notes',    field: 'notes',    minWidth: 260, responsive: 3 }  // collapses first
  ]
});
```

### 15.2 FullCalendar (7.x core, verified against 7.0.2)

```html
<!-- verified against FullCalendar 7.0.2 -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/fullcalendar@7.0.2/skeleton.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/fullcalendar@7.0.2/themes/classic/theme.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/fullcalendar@7.0.2/themes/classic/palette.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/1978io/78UIKit@v0.3.0/css/adapters/fullcalendar.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/fullcalendar@7.0.2/all/global.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/fullcalendar@7.0.2/themes/classic/global.js"></script>
```

Core only — nothing here assumes a premium plugin. v7 ships **hashed atomic class names** (the calendar
root looks like `fc-classic-dl1 fc-classic-1sP …`, and those strings change between builds), so
class-level overrides are off the table: the palette custom properties are the whole supported theming
surface, and remapping them onto kit tokens is all this adapter does. A legacy block at the bottom of the
file covers v6.x, which still had stable class names. Everything resolves at runtime, so the calendar
re-themes the instant `data-theme` flips.

### 15.3 Chart.js (4.x, verified against 4.5.1)

```html
<!-- verified against Chart.js 4.5.1 -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js@4.5.1/dist/chart.umd.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/1978io/78UIKit@v0.3.0/js/_78.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/1978io/78UIKit@v0.3.0/js/adapters/chartjs.js"></script>
```

This one is JS because a chart is a `<canvas>`, and canvas pixels cannot resolve `var(--accent)` — colors
are baked in at draw time. So the adapter reads the tokens with `getComputedStyle`, pushes them into
`Chart.defaults` (font, text, grid and axis colors, legend, title, tooltip styled as a kit card, element
borders), and — the part everyone misses — re-applies them and calls `update('none')` on **every live
chart** whenever `_78:themechange` fires, because `Chart.defaults` is only read when a chart is
*constructed*. Load order matters: with the adapter in place before your charts are built, they are
constructed already themed rather than corrected afterwards.

On a live switch the scales follow too: Chart.js binds each scale's colors once, so the adapter rewrites
grid, axis-line, tick and title colors on every live scale — but only values that still equal the previous
theme's token, so a color a chart set for itself is never overwritten. *(Fixed in 0.3.0: before it, the
grid and tick labels kept the old theme until a reload.)*

**Don't set theme colors per chart.** `plugins.legend.labels.color`, `scales.x.grid.color` and friends in
a chart's own options out-rank `Chart.defaults` and are read once, so they stay on the theme the page
loaded in. Leave them unset and the legend (`--text`), ticks (`--dim`) and grid (`--border`) follow every
switch. If one chart genuinely needs its own color, re-set it on `_78:themechange`.

It also registers a plugin that colors datasets from the theme.

**Dataset ownership rule:** a dataset that declares **no** `backgroundColor` and **no** `borderColor` is
adopted and recolored on every theme switch. A dataset that declares either one is **never touched** —
your explicit color always wins. Force it either way with `$_78: true` / `$_78: false` on the dataset.

```js
// adopted: no colors declared → themed, and re-themed on every switch
new Chart(ctx, {
  type: 'line',
  data: { labels: days, datasets: [{ label: 'Revenue', data: revenue }] }
});

// left alone forever: it declares its own color
new Chart(ctx2, {
  type: 'bar',
  data: { labels: days, datasets: [{ label: 'Budget', data: budget, backgroundColor: '#888' }] }
});
```

**The series ramp.** The first dataset gets `--accent`; the second gets `--series-2`, a true gray (no
hue, so it recedes behind any accent and can never sit near it in hue); the third onward get the six
categorical tones (`--cat-1` … `--cat-6`, §2.9). The semantic colors are not used for series: a series
is a kind of thing, not a state, and a green line reads as "good". *(Changed in 0.3.0 — the ramp used to be
accent, success, warn, danger, info, dim, so an existing chart's second and later series change color.
Pin a dataset's color explicitly to keep the old look.)* The theme generator outputs `--series-2` too.

Series coloring by chart type: line and radar get a solid border, a 16%-alpha fill and matching points;
pie, doughnut and polar area get a per-slice palette with `--bg2` separators (polar area at 70% alpha);
bar, bubble, scatter and everything else get a solid fill with an 80%-alpha hover.

```js
_78.adapters.chartjs.palette(5)     // → 5 series colors from the current theme:
                                    //   --accent, --series-2, --cat-1 … --cat-6,
                                    //   then the same ramp again at 65% and 40% alpha
_78.adapters.chartjs.tokens()       // → { text, dim, border, bg2, bg3, accent, success, warn,
                                    //     danger, info, series2, cats: [6], font, fontSize,
                                    //     radius } as resolved now
_78.adapters.chartjs.alpha('#4b9eff', .16)   // → 'rgba(75,158,255,0.16)' — the `-lo` idea, in JS
_78.adapters.chartjs.apply()        // re-read tokens, restyle defaults, update every live chart
_78.adapters.chartjs.plugin         // the registered plugin object, id '_78palette'
```

`alpha()` handles `#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`, `rgb()` and `rgba()`, and returns anything else
untouched rather than mangling it. Chart.js 4's own auto-color plugin is disabled — the adapter replaces
it.

---

## 16. Theme generator — `_78.gen`

`js/generator.js` derives the **whole token set for light and dark** from one accent color, with live WCAG
checks, an apply-to-the-page mode and a shareable URL. It is opt-in and **not** part of `_78.js` — load it
only where you need it (the tool itself lives at https://78uikit.com).

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/1978io/78UIKit@v0.3.0/js/_78.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/1978io/78UIKit@v0.3.0/js/generator.js"></script>
```

Two rules the file exists to enforce: **work in OKLCH** (HSL ramps go muddy — equal steps in HSL are not
equal steps to the eye), and **dark is not inverted light** (each theme gets its own lightness and chroma
targets). No color library, no build — both sRGB ⇄ OKLCH directions are implemented in the file, plus a
chroma-reduction gamut map for OKLCH values that land outside sRGB.

### 16.1 The config

```js
{
  accent:  '#0073ea',   // any hex; invalid input falls back to the default
  neutral: 'neutral',   // 'neutral' | 'cool' | 'warm' | 'accent' — the tint of the grays
  radius:  8,           // 0–20 px; --radius-sm/-lg are derived from it
  density: 'cozy'       // 'compact' | 'cozy' | 'comfortable' — spacing scale + control heights
}
```

`_78.gen.DEFAULTS` holds exactly that object. Density drives the `--space-*` scale (×0.75 / ×1 / ×1.25)
and `--control-h` / `--control-h-sm` / `--icon-btn-size` (32/26/28, 36/28/32, 40/32/36).

### 16.2 Deriving and emitting

```js
var result = _78.gen.derive({ accent: '#7c5cff', neutral: 'cool', radius: 10, density: 'cozy' });

result.config    // the normalized config
result.accent    // the accent as {l, c, h} in OKLCH
result.light     // { '--bg': '…', '--text': '…', … } — the full light color token set
result.dark      // the same for dark
result.base      // the non-color tokens density and radius imply
result.notes     // human-readable notes about any automatic contrast nudges

var css = _78.gen.css(result);                 // paste-ready CSS: both theme blocks + the base block
var css = _78.gen.css(result, { base: false }); // color only, leaving shape/density alone

var block = _78.gen.block(':root[data-theme="dark"]', result.dark, true);  // one block; true = grouped
```

The categories are derived too, on fixed hues like the semantics (a category must not change meaning
when the accent does); only their lightness is fitted per theme. Every generated theme includes all six.

`css()` output drops straight into a `<style>` after `kit.css` and re-themes everything — components,
adapters and all.

### 16.3 Contrast report

```js
var rows = _78.gen.report(result.dark, 'dark');
// [{ label: '--text on --bg', ratio: 12.4, need: 4.5, large: false, soft: false, pass: true }, …]
```

The pairs that decide whether a theme is usable: `--text` on each of the three surfaces, `--dim` on
`--bg2`, `--accent-text` on `--accent`, `--accent` on `--bg2` (large-text threshold, 3:1), each semantic
color and each category (`--cat-1` … `--cat-6`) on its own `-lo` tint, and `--border` on `--bg2` as an advisory check (`soft: true` — an edge you
cannot see is a border that is not doing its job). Lightness is nudged automatically where a pair would
otherwise fail; the nudges land in `result.notes`.

### 16.4 Apply, persist, share

```js
_78.gen.apply(result);     // inject the CSS as <style id="_78-gen-style">, persist it, set data-_78-gen
_78.gen.clear();           // remove the style, clear storage, drop the attribute
_78.gen.stored();          // → the saved config, or null

_78.gen.preview(el, result.light, result.base);   // write one theme's tokens onto a container as inline
                                                  // custom properties — e.g. show light inside a dark page
```

`apply()` writes a real stylesheet rather than inline properties, so **both** theme blocks are present and
the kit's own toggle keeps working. It stores `{ config, css }` under `localStorage['_78-gen']` and fires
`_78:genchange` on `document` (`e.detail.config`, `null` after `clear()`).

`_78.gen.PREPAINT` is a second pre-paint snippet that puts a saved generated theme back before the first
paint with no re-derivation. It runs **after** `_78.theme`'s snippet and before any stylesheet.

### 16.5 The `?theme=` URL format

`accent.neutral.radius.density`, hex without the `#` — e.g. `?theme=0073ea.cool.8.cozy`. Short, readable,
no backend.

```js
_78.gen.encode(config)        // → '0073ea.cool.8.cozy'
_78.gen.decode('7c5cff.warm.10.compact')   // → a normalized config object
_78.gen.fromUrl()             // read ?theme= from location.search → config or null
_78.gen.shareUrl(config)      // → the current URL with ?theme= set
_78.gen.STORAGE               // '_78-gen'
```

### 16.6 Color math, exposed

`_78.gen` also exposes the primitives it is built on, in case you need them:
`resolve(color)` → `{r,g,b}` · `toOklch(rgb)` · `fromOklch(l, c, h)` · `oklch(l, c, h)` (formats the CSS
string) · `hex(rgb)` · `rgba(rgb, a)` · `luminance(rgb)` · `contrast(a, b)` · `over(color, alpha, backdrop)`
(what a tint actually looks like over a surface).

---

## 17. Events, storage keys and file map

### Events

| Event | Fires on | `e.detail` |
|---|---|---|
| `_78:themechange` | `document` | `{ theme: 'dark'\|'light', pref: 'dark'\|'light'\|'system' }` |
| `_78:railchange` | `document` | `{ rail: boolean }` |
| `_78:drawerchange` | `document` | `{ open: boolean }` |
| `_78:tabchange` | the `._78-tabs` list (bubbles) | `{ index, tab, panel, id }` |
| `_78:segchange` | the `._78-seg` group (bubbles) | `{ index, button, value }` |
| `_78:genchange` | `document` | `{ config }` — `null` after `_78.gen.clear()` |

### localStorage keys

| Key | Written by | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `_78-theme` | `_78.theme` | `'dark'` \| `'light'` \| `'system'` |
| `_78-sidebar` | `_78.shell` | `'full'` \| `'rail'` |
| `_78-gen` | `_78.gen` | `{ config, css }` as JSON |

Every read and write is wrapped in `try` / `catch` — private mode or blocked storage degrades, it never
throws.

### `<html>` attributes

`data-theme` · `data-theme-pref` · `data-sidebar` · `data-drawer` · `data-_78-gen`

### Files

```
css/  kit.css              the one stylesheet a project links (@imports everything below)
      tokens.css           light + dark color blocks + the shared non-color tokens
      reset.css            minimal reset, themed scrollbars, focus ring
      components/          shell · buttons · cards · forms · switch · seg · details · badges · meta ·
                           viz · figure · split-bar · table · tabs · modal · toast · alert · notes ·
                           theme-toggle · utilities
      adapters/            tabulator.css · fullcalendar.css — opt-in, never in kit.css
js/   _78.js               _78.theme · _78.tone · _78.util · _78.shell · _78.modal · _78.notify · _78.tabs · _78.seg ·
                           _78.viz
      generator.js         _78.gen — opt-in, not part of _78.js
      adapters/            chartjs.js — _78.adapters.chartjs
demo/                      living examples, every page in light + dark
llms.txt · llms-full.txt   this reference, for AI coding assistants
```

- https://78uikit.com — docs, the live component gallery, and the theme generator
- https://github.com/1978io/78UIKit — source, releases, changelog, MIT license
